title: Berkeley prohibition on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or occupancy
requirement: Landlords may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm (one using nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old) to set rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. Vendors may not sell, license, or provide such algorithms to Berkeley landlords.
key_value: Ban; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (each month and each unit a separate violation)
coverage_conditions: All landlords setting rents or occupancy levels for residential units in Berkeley, and vendors providing coordinated pricing algorithms to them.
exemptions: Products publishing aggregated, anonymous data without recommending rents; products used to set rents or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; market research for financing, appraisals, or software research/testing/training if competitor data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only if the landlord uses a coordinated pricing algorithm relying on nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old.

citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.63 (§§ 13.63.030, 13.63.040), as amended by Ord. No. 7,992-N.S.
quoted_span:
B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.
conflict_note: Official ordinance text shows amending Ord. 7,992-N.S. passed to print 2025-11-18 (second reading 2025-12-02) with no effective date; secondary sources give January 2026. Original Chapter 13.63 predates the amendment. RealPage v. City of Berkeley was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice 2026-01-14.

title: Required Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement
requirement: An owner charging an application or credit-report fee must give a Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement before receiving the fee and state the maximum fee permitted under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b).
coverage_conditions: Owners or agents of Berkeley residential property who charge screening or application fees.
quoted_span: The “Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement” shall mean the following statement or a substantially similar statement:
conflict_note: The statement's required URL is still to be provided by the City; no effective date stated.

title: Ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies
requirement: Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate's departure or adding/replacing a roommate; contrary lease terms are unenforceable.
coverage_conditions: All Berkeley residential rental agreements, including existing leases.
quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

title: Owner move-in eviction relocation assistance (2026 amounts, annually CPI-adjusted)
requirement: Owners evicting for owner move-in must pay relocation assistance. Measure BB requires the Rent Board to adjust the amounts for inflation each year.
coverage_conditions: Tenants in Berkeley units covered by the Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance evicted for owner move-in.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only when an owner move-in eviction occurs; qualifying-household criteria not stated.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance (relocation provisions), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction.
conflict_note: Effective date refers to the 2026 inflation adjustment approved by the Rent Board 2025-10-16, not the original enactment.

title: Ellis Act withdrawal relocation assistance (2026 amounts)
requirement: Owners evicting tenants to withdraw a property from the rental market must pay the same relocation assistance as for owner move-in evictions.
coverage_conditions: Berkeley tenants evicted under an Ellis Act withdrawal.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to Ellis Act withdrawal evictions; qualifying-household criteria not stated.

quoted_span: The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires the same relocation assistance payments for tenants evicted so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market.
conflict_note: Date refers to the 2026 inflation adjustment, not original enactment.

title: Berkeley just cause required for evictions from fully or partially covered units
requirement: Tenants in units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted without just cause.
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units: pre-1980 multifamily, single-family homes (any tenancy date), rooming houses, post-June-1980 new construction, most condominiums, subsidized units.
exemptions: Golden Duplex owner-occupied since 1979-12-31 and currently; shared kitchen/bath with an owner resident at tenancy start; tenancies after 2018-11-07 on owner-occupied ADU properties; university dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy (Golden Duplex, shared kitchen/bath, ADU); ADU tenancy start date; dormitory or cooperative status.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).
conflict_note: No code citation or original enactment date in sources. State just cause (Civ. Code 1946.2) yields where this local ordinance applies.

title: No nonpayment eviction for rental debt under one month's Fair Market Rent (Measure BB)
requirement: Eviction for nonpayment is allowed only if rental debt is at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent for an equivalent unit in the Oakland-Fremont HUD Metro FMR area.
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: Eviction for nonpayment of rent is no longer permitted for rental debt of less than one month’s Fair Market Rent for a unit of equivalent size.
conflict_note: Measure BB effective date not stated.

title: No eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar lease (Measure BB)
requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease when a fixed-term lease expires.
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.
conflict_note: Measure BB effective date not stated.

title: Stricter requirements for lease-violation evictions (Measure BB)
requirement: Lease-breach evictions require a mutually agreed material term, actual harm to the landlord, and proof the tenant's behavior was unreasonable; notices must clearly describe the breach.
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: In any notice terminating a tenancy for a lease breach, the landlord must clearly describe the alleged breach. The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant’s behavior was unreasonable, and may not evict tenants for lease breaches that do not cause the landlord any actual harm.
conflict_note: Measure BB effective date not stated.

title: Eviction notice content and three-business-day filing with Rent Board
requirement: Termination notices must reference Rent Board counseling; copies of termination notices, notices to quit, and summons and complaints must be filed with the Rent Board within three business days of service.
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: The landlord must file with the Rent Board a copy of any notice to terminate a tenancy, notice to quit, and summons and complaint no later than three business days after the tenant was served with the document.
conflict_note: Measure BB effective date not stated.

title: Berkeley rent ceilings and Annual General Adjustment (AGA), capped at 5% by Measure BB
requirement: For fully covered units, landlords may raise rent ceilings only by the Rent Board's Annual General Adjustment (65% of Bay Area CPI change), capped at 5% under Measure BB (banked AGAs may exceed 5% to reach the ceiling). The 2026 AGA is 1.0%, effective no earlier than 2026-01-01, for eligible landlords who give required notice. Government-owned/subsidized units are now fully or partially covered.
key_value: 2026 AGA 1.0%; AGA = 65% of CPI change, max 5%
coverage_conditions: Fully covered units: most units in multifamily properties built before 1980 (no rent control where Certificate of Occupancy issued after June 1980), single-family homes with tenancies beginning before 1996, rooming houses with 5+ individually rented rooms, and fully covered subsidized units (Section 8 vouchers, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC, HOME).
exemptions: Partially covered (no rent ceiling): post-June-1980 new construction, single-family homes with tenancies from 1996-01-01, most condominiums, Section 202/811 units, and certain HUD-mortgaged project-based units. Fully exempt: Golden Duplex owner-occupied since 1979-12-31; shared kitchen/bath with owner resident at tenancy start; tenancies after 2018-11-07 on owner-occupied ADU properties; dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives. 2026 AGA does not apply to tenancies beginning on or after 2025-01-01 with rents set under Costa-Hawkins.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Single-family tenancy start date (before 1996); condominium status; Golden Duplex, shared kitchen/bath, and ADU owner-occupancy exemptions; subsidy type and HUD mortgage status; Regulation 1148 eligibility and notice; Costa-Hawkins tenancies beginning on or after 2025-01-01.

citation: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.76.110A; Rent Board Regulation 1148; Berkeley Rent Ordinance as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span:
At its regular meeting on October 16, 2025, the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board 
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026.
conflict_note: Sources describe the cutoff both as 'built before 1980' and as Certificate of Occupancy 'after June 1980'; the June 1980 CofO cutoff is used. Measure BB's effective date is not stated. Effective date shown is for the 2026 AGA. State AB 1482 cap yields to this stricter local rent control.

title: Rent increase petitions only for completed capital improvements (Measure BB)
requirement: Landlords may petition for rent increases only for completed capital improvements; preliminary authorization for planned improvements is no longer available.
coverage_conditions: Fully covered units subject to rent ceilings.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unit must be fully covered by the Rent Ordinance.

citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: Landlords can only file a petition for rent increases for completed capital improvements (they can no longer petition to have rent increases preliminarily authorized for planned capital improvements).
conflict_note: Measure BB effective date not stated.

title: Utility charges must be in base rent unless separately metered (Measure BB)
requirement: For tenancies starting on or after 2024-02-06 in fully covered units, utilities may be charged only as a set amount in base rent, or where separately metered and in the tenant's name per the lease. Adding utility costs to the ceiling requires a Rent Board petition.
coverage_conditions: Fully covered units; tenancies starting on or after 2024-02-06.
exemptions: Separately metered utilities in the tenant's name as required by the lease.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenancy start date on or after 2024-02-06; utility metering arrangement; unit fully covered.

citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
quoted_span: Utility charges must be a set amount incorporated into the base rent at the start of a tenancy unless the utility is separately metered and the account is in the tenant’s name as specified in the lease.
conflict_note: The 2024-02-06 applicability date predates the November 2024 election passing Measure BB; may be retroactive application or an error on the source page.

title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decisions, including refusing to rent, terminating, or charging higher rent or deposit based on criminal history.
key_value: Criminal history inquiries and use banned; fines $1,000-$10,000 per violation
coverage_conditions: Current and prospective tenants of rental housing in Berkeley.
exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner lives as primary residence; owner move-back agreements under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner residence in 1-3 unit property; public housing/Section 8 status; owner move-back agreements; roommate/sublet situations.

quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
conflict_note: Source gives only the Council passage date (2020-04-14), not the effective date; treated as in force because the Rent Board administers complaints.

title: Annual interest on security deposits (Berkeley Rent Ordinance)
requirement: Landlords of fully or partially covered units must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the end of each year, prorated if the tenant moves out mid-year.
coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
exemptions: Golden Duplex; shared kitchen/bath with resident owner; post-2018-11-07 tenancies on owner-occupied ADU properties; dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy exemptions; dormitory/cooperative status.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.
conflict_note: Interest rate and code section not given.

title: Boston tenant eviction protections home rule petition (H.3744) - not enacted
requirement: Would have authorized Boston to implement tenant eviction protections; sent to a study order 2024-09-09 and not enacted. Not law.
coverage_conditions: Boston residential tenants (proposed).
quoted_span: that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.
conflict_note: 193rd session ended without enactment.

title: Housing Stability Notification Act: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources
requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with the notice to quit or non-renewal, and file a copy with the City.
key_value: Notice with every notice to quit/non-renewal; $300/day for 2nd+ offense
coverage_conditions: All Boston landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy.
exemptions: Hospitals, skilled nursing/health facilities, nonprofit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only when a tenancy is being terminated or not renewed.

citation: City of Boston Housing Stability Notification Act (Oct. 2020); penalties Sec. 10-11.7
quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.
conflict_note: Notice requirement only; not a just-cause standard and violations do not halt eviction. Categorized as closest fit.

title: Boston rent stabilization home rule petition (H.3744, 193rd session) - not enacted
requirement: Would have authorized Boston to implement rent stabilization; sent to a study order (H5035) 2024-09-09 and died at session end. Not law.
coverage_conditions: Boston residential rental housing (proposed).
quoted_span: that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.
conflict_note: Local rent control remains barred by M.G.L. c. 40P absent state enactment.

title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy: criminal history limits
requirement: Covered providers may not use blanket bans and must assess applicants individually; they may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed/expunged records, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old.
key_value: Convictions older than 5 years may not be considered
coverage_conditions: Housing receiving Boston DND funding and/or land, or BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units.
exemptions: Direct relationship to the housing sought or unreasonable safety risk; current criminal behavior; conflicting federal/state requirements preempt.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to DND-funded or IDP income-restricted housing.

citation: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development, Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
quoted_span: a) Arrests that did not result in conviction.
conflict_note: Administrative policy applied through funding/IDP agreements, not a general ordinance; current status not confirmed.

title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy: credit score and history limits
requirement: Covered providers may not use credit scores to approve or deny; credit history may be used only in lieu of unavailable rental history, and lack of credit history is not grounds for rejection.
coverage_conditions: Housing receiving Boston DND funding and/or land, or BPDA IDP income-restricted units.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to DND-funded or IDP income-restricted housing.

citation: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development, Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
quoted_span: a) The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing
conflict_note: Administrative policy; current status not confirmed.

title: Boston fair housing ban including rental assistance discrimination
requirement: Landlords may not discriminate against applicants or tenants based on protected classes including rental assistance (e.g., Section 8), family status, and military status.
coverage_conditions: Any housing rented, sold, or financed in Boston.
citation: City of Boston fair housing law, enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission (section not stated)
quoted_span: In the City of Boston, it’s illegal to discriminate when renting, buying, selling, or securing financing for any housing.
conflict_note: Summary page; no ordinance citation, effective date, or exemptions; commission also enforces state/federal law.

title: Cartwright Act ban on using or distributing a common pricing algorithm as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade (AB 325)
requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (used by two or more persons and using competitor data to recommend, set, or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade. Applies generally, including rental pricing.
key_value: Prohibition; criminal fines up to greater of $6M or 2x gain/loss (corporations), civil fines up to $1M per violation
coverage_conditions: Any person other than the end consumer, including landlords and rental software providers.
exemptions: End consumers; single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires use of a common pricing algorithm as part of an agreement restraining trade.

citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(a) (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
conflict_note: Chaptered 2025-10-06; 2026-01-01 effective date inferred from California's default rule and confirmed by secondary source. General antitrust law, not housing-specific; operates alongside local bans.

title: Cartwright Act ban on coercing adoption of common pricing algorithm recommendations (AB 325)
requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm while coercing another to adopt a price or commercial term it recommends for the same or similar products or services in California.
key_value: Prohibition on coercing adoption of algorithm-recommended prices or terms
coverage_conditions: Any person other than the end consumer using or distributing a common pricing algorithm.
exemptions: End consumers; single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires coercion to adopt algorithm recommendations.

citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(b) (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
quoted_span: (b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.
conflict_note: Effective date inferred from default rule; what constitutes coercion is left to courts.

title: Application screening fee capped at actual costs and $30 (CPI-adjusted)
requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket costs plus reasonable value of time, and never more than $30 per applicant adjusted annually for CPI since 1998-01-01.
key_value: Max $30/applicant CPI-adjusted; $68.96 for 2026 (per Berkeley Rent Board)
coverage_conditions: Landlords or agents of residential rental property charging applicants (including guarantors/cosigners) a screening fee.
exemptions: Does not preempt deposit/fee rules of federal or state housing assistance programs.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Housing-assistance program fee rules may govern instead.

citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b) (as amended by Stats. 2025, ch. 67, AB 1170)
quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
conflict_note: Current text effective 2026-01-01 (AB 1170), but the $30 CPI-adjusted cap predates it; original effective date not in corpus. The $68.96 2026 figure comes from the Berkeley Rent Board.

title: No screening fee when no unit is available
requirement: A landlord may not charge a screening fee when it knows or should have known that no unit is available now or within a reasonable time.
coverage_conditions: Landlords or agents of residential rental property charging screening fees.
quoted_span: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.
conflict_note: Current text effective 2026-01-01 (AB 1170); the provision existed earlier in some form, original date not in corpus.

title: Screening fee allowed only with first-in-time process or full refund to non-selected applicants
requirement: A landlord may collect a screening fee only if it offers either (A) a first-in-time process under written criteria approving the first qualified applicant and charging only when an application is considered, or (B) refunds to non-selected applicants within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission.
key_value: Refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission; 7-day refund for inadvertent concurrent fees
coverage_conditions: Landlords or agents of residential rental property collecting screening fees.
exemptions: No refund under the first-in-time option for applicants denied after consideration for failing screening criteria.
quoted_span: A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only if the landlord or their agent, at the time the application screening fee is collected, offers any of the following:
conflict_note: Effective date taken from the AB 1170 amendment note; attribution of subdivision (c)(2) to that amendment is inferred.

title: Itemized receipt and return of unused screening fee
requirement: The landlord must give the applicant a receipt itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent, and return any portion not used for authorized screening.
coverage_conditions: Landlords or agents collecting an application screening fee.
quoted_span: (d) The landlord or their agent shall provide, personally, or by mail, the applicant with a receipt for the fee paid by the applicant, which receipt shall itemize the out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord or their agent to obtain and process the information about the applicant.
conflict_note: Current text effective 2026-01-01 (AB 1170); original date not in corpus.

title: Copy of credit report to fee-paying applicant within seven days
requirement: If an applicant paid a screening fee, the landlord must provide a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of receiving it.
coverage_conditions: Landlords or agents collecting an application screening fee.
quoted_span: (f) If an application screening fee has been paid by the applicant, the landlord or their agent shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.
conflict_note: Current text effective 2026-01-01 (AB 1170); original date not in corpus.

title: Tenant Protection Act statewide just cause eviction requirement (Civ. Code 1946.2)
requirement: After a tenant has lawfully occupied for 12 months (24 months if adult tenants were added), the owner may terminate only for a listed at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. No-fault terminations require relocation assistance equal to one month's rent (payment within 15 days or waiver of final month's rent).
key_value: Just cause after 12 months; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent
coverage_conditions: Residential real property, including mobilehome park units, after 12/24 months of occupancy, where no qualifying local just cause ordinance applies.
exemptions: Transient hotels; nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities; dormitories; shared bath/kitchen with resident owner; owner-occupied single-family homes renting up to two units/bedrooms; owner-occupied duplexes (no ADU/JADU); certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable units not owned by a REIT, corporation, or corporate-member LLC with required exemption notice; deed-restricted affordable housing; mobilehome homeowners; properties under a qualifying local just cause ordinance.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Occupancy duration; for separately alienable units, owner entity type and exemption notice; owner occupancy; deed-restricted affordable housing; whether a local just cause ordinance applies.

interaction: Yields to a stricter local rule in the same category where one covers the unit.
quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
conflict_note: Effective date is the operative date of the current text; original AB 1482 protections date to 2020. Last amended by AB 1529 effective 2026-01-01; repealed 2030-01-01. Yields to local just cause ordinances adopted on or before 2019-09-01 or more protective later ordinances.

title: Temporary relocation payments for capital improvement displacement under 20 days (San Francisco)
requirement: Relocation for temporary capital improvement displacements in San Francisco lasting less than 20 days is governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9 rather than SF Rent Ordinance § 37.9C.
key_value: $446/day plus actual moving expenses (3/1/26-2/28/27, per SF Rent Board)
coverage_conditions: Temporary capital improvement evictions in San Francisco lasting less than 20 days.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Temporary capital improvement displacement under 20 days.

quoted_span: *The amount of relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions for less than 20 days is governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 and not by Rent Ordinance Section 37.9C.
conflict_note: The daily amount is from the SF Rent Board current-rates page (c175).

title: California statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act, Civ. Code 1947.12)
requirement: Over any 12-month period, gross rent may not rise more than 5% plus regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, measured from the lowest rent in the prior 12 months; at most two increases per 12 months.
coverage_conditions: Residential real property (incl. mobilehome park units) not subject to stricter local rent control and not exempt.
exemptions: Certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing; dormitories; stricter local rent control; separately alienable units (single-family homes, condos) not owned by a REIT, corporation, or corporate-member LLC with written exemption notice; owner-occupied duplexes (no ADU/JADU) where owner lived there at tenancy start; mobilehome homeowners.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner entity type and exemption notice for separately alienable units; owner-occupied duplex; affordable-housing restrictions; dormitory status; whether stricter local rent control applies.

interaction: Yields to a stricter local rule in the same category where one covers the unit.
quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
conflict_note: Applies to increases on or after 2019-03-15 (mobilehomes 2021-02-18); current text re-added by SB 567, operative 2024-04-01; repealed 2030-01-01. Yields where stricter local rent control applies.

title: FEHA and Civil Rights Council limits on criminal history in tenant screening
requirement: Housing providers may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not impose blanket bans on people with criminal histories; conviction-based denials must be directly related to tenancy suitability.
key_value: No arrest-only, sealed/expunged, or juvenile records; no blanket bans
coverage_conditions: Most California housing providers, including landlords, property managers, and tenant screening companies.
exemptions: Owner-occupied homes renting to one additional person (discriminatory advertising still barred); certain shared-living, senior, and homeless youth housing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy exemption when renting to one additional person.

citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act; Civil Rights Council (formerly FEHC) criminal history housing regulations
quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
conflict_note: 2020-01-01 is the regulations' effective date per a secondary trade-association source; no regulation section number given.

title: FEHA housing discrimination ban including source of income (Section 8 / vouchers)
requirement: Owners may not discriminate against or harass any person, including in screening (also by third-party screening companies), based on protected characteristics including source of income; since 2020-01-01 (SB 329) source of income includes housing subsidies such as Section 8, so 'No Section 8' policies and refusing subsidy paperwork are prohibited.
key_value: Ban on refusing Section 8 / housing vouchers
coverage_conditions: Owners of any housing accommodation in California and those advertising rentals; tenant screening companies.
exemptions: Owner-occupied homes renting to one additional person (advertising still barred); shared-living single-sex preference; qualifying senior housing; some homeless youth housing. Inquiries into level or source of income are allowed.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy and senior housing exemptions.

quoted_span: (a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
conflict_note: 2020-01-01 is when SB 329 extended source of income to housing subsidies; the underlying source-of-income protection is older. Last amended by SB 267 effective 2024-01-01.

title: Credit history use for subsidized applicants requires alternative-evidence option (SB 267)
requirement: Where a government rent subsidy is involved, a housing provider may not use an applicant's credit history unless it offers the option to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay the tenant's portion of rent.
key_value: Must offer alternative-evidence option before using credit history
coverage_conditions: Rental applications involving a government rent subsidy.
